subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds
body:
From: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

Hey Sean,

We’re ready to merge the new Dedicated autoscaling correctness dashboards + alerts (ENG-2846 / observability-pack PR #842) but want SRE leadership approval on the paging thresholds + ownership before we enable pages in prod.

Summary of proposed pages (prod only, Dedicated pools w/ bounded autoscaling flag):
1) Bound violation (should be impossible): page immediately
   - Alert: dedicated_autoscaler_bound_violation_total > 0 (5m)
   - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool_id (pool_id only in event log; not in metrics)
2) Scaling lag: page if sustained impact to p95 latency attributable to pending scale-up
   - Alert: scale_up_actuation_lag_seconds p95 > 180s for 15m AND queue_depth > threshold
3) Oscillation: page if controller is flapping and impacting requests
   - Alert: scale_events_total{direction=~"up|down"} high rate w/ clamp activity for 30m

Non-paging (ticket / Slack notification):
- Forecast pipeline unhealthy
- Confidence gating disabled
- Clamp rate high (indicates max too low / min too high)

Questions we need your call on:
- Do we page on oscillation at all, or keep it ticket-only until after GA?
- Confirm owning team for (a) bound violation, (b) scaling lag, (c) forecast pipeline issues.

Attachment has the full thresholds + links to the intended runbooks.

Thanks,
Aisha

—
Aisha Bello
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dedicated-autoscaling-alerts-v2.pdf (PDF)



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:04 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

Aisha,

Thanks — directionally good, but I’m concerned we’re going to create noise in week 1.

Requests before we turn paging on:

1) Reduce false positives / de-page anything that’s not “customer impact + actionable”
- Bound violation: yes, page. (Should be 0; if >0 we have a correctness bug.)
- Scaling lag: I want this expressed in a way that maps to customer impact. Can we gate on elevated p95 latency + evidence of pending scale-up (e.g., desired>applied for N minutes) instead of queue depth alone?
- Oscillation: do NOT page initially. Make this ticket-only + dashboard; we can revisit once we see baseline rates and have tuned cooldown defaults.

2) Confirm ownership + routing
We need a single clear owner per page.
- Bound violation / clamp correctness: Fleet autoscaler team should be primary, SRE secondary.
- Scaling lag pages: SRE primary (it’s a customer impact symptom), Fleet autoscaler team secondary.
- Forecast pipeline: no pages at launch; notify in #eng-sre + file ticket to Applied ML.

3) Cardinality and labels
Please ensure we don’t put pool_id or customer_id on paging metrics. Those belong in the event/audit stream only.

If you can revise with the above, I’ll approve enabling pages.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Org Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:21 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

+1 to Sean’s point on cardinality.

One more ask: for the actuation lag metric, keep labels to {region, hardware_class, service_tier}. If we need pool-level forensics, do it via the structured decision logs (clamp_reason, desired_replicas, applied_replicas) and link from the alert to the “Scaling Decision” dashboard.

Allison

—
Allison Grant
Observability Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

On ownership: agreed Fleet should own bound violations/correctness issues.

For scaling lag: I’d prefer Fleet be secondary and only paged if there’s evidence of “stuck actuation” (desired != applied) rather than general latency. Otherwise we’ll get paged for normal demand spikes where max bounds are doing what the customer asked.

If we can add a hint in the alert text like:
- “If clamp_reason=max_bound and throttles increasing, this is likely customer max too low → CS guidance”
- “If desired>applied with no clamp, likely provisioning/actuation issue → Fleet”

…that will reduce ping-pong.

Vanessa

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Fleet Manager, Redwood Inference



From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 1:47 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

Made updates per feedback and pushed a new revision to the PR + doc.

Changes:
- Oscillation: removed from paging; now “ticket-only” with dashboard panel + annotation.
- Scaling lag page condition: now requires ALL of:
  (a) p95 latency burn indicator elevated (10m),
  (b) desired_replicas > applied_replicas for 10m (no scale-down in progress),
  (c) clamp_reason != max_bound (so we don’t page when customer intentionally capped),
  (d) requests_throttled > 0 OR queue_time_p95 elevated
- Label cleanup: removed any pool-level labels from metrics. Pool_id only in decision events.
- Alert text includes routing guidance:
  - If clamp_reason=max_bound → link to customer guidance + Console “Scaling History”
  - If desired>applied + no clamp → link to Fleet runbook section “stuck actuation/provisioning”

Open item: what should we set as the paging threshold for (b) desired>applied? (10m now.) We can tighten later.

Attaching the runbook link list we plan to include in the alert annotations.

Rafael

—
Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: autoscaling-slo-alerts-runbook-links.txt (text)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 4, 2026 at 4:37 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated autoscaling SLO alerts — request for approval of paging thresholds

Approved with the revisions Rafael listed.

Decision / final calls:
- Bound violation: page (Fleet primary, SRE secondary). Must stay at 0.
- Scaling lag: page with the “desired>applied + customer-impact gate” as implemented (SRE primary, Fleet secondary).
- Oscillation: ticket-only until we have baseline + tuning.
- Forecast pipeline: no paging at launch; Slack notify + ticket.

Please add one more thing before enabling in prod:
- Explicit “owner” line in the alert annotations (PagerDuty service + escalation policy) so there’s no ambiguity.

Once that’s in, you have a go-ahead to enable pages for the allowlisted bounded-autoscaling pools only.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Org Lead, Redwood Inference
